long_biography.plain_text:
A traditional wooden schooner gave Hercules Vlachodimitris a platform to demonstrate how engineering and styling could be developed together. Working with interior designer Lally Poulias, he shaped the exterior around classic Greek proportions while insisting that seaworthiness, family use and the facilities of a large cruiser remain fundamental.

His wife, Liana, contributed substantially to the project. Modern stabilisation and hotel systems were incorporated discreetly, while custom deck fittings carried visual motifs across functional elements. The project illustrated a hands-on method in which technical decisions, construction detail and life at sea were treated as one design rather than separate layers.
